newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia agrees sale of strategic metals plant.
newsitem.headline: Estonia agrees sale of strategic metals plant.

text.p: The Estonian Privatisation Agency (EPA) on Wednesday agreed to sell a majority stake in Estonia's key strategic metals plant Silmet to a company that includes one of the country's largest consortia.
The EPA decided to sell 65 percent of Silmet, a former Soviet defence industry plant, to EPHAG, Margus Linnemae, chairman of EPHAG, told Reuters.
Linname is also head of Magnum Group, which is a consortium that spans businesses from pharmaceuticals to brewing. He would not say how much Silmet was sold for.
Magnum owns 40 percent of EPHAG while the rest is owned by a private investor.
Silmet had turnover of 185 million kroons in 1995 but made a loss. It processes rare earth metals and is one of the dozen or so plants of it type in the world.
But it lost its main customer, the Soviet defence industry. Silmet has recently begun to export metals to Japan and Russia.
Any buyer of Silmet also faces the problems of cleaning up the environmental mess left around the plant.
A final deal between EPHAG and the privatisation agency will probably be concluded in around one month.
